reason: Partly refuted. The numbers match check_coord_refiner.json (a0.5 +0.00215, a0.3 -0.00125, a1.0 -0.00498, division TP change 0), and so does V1284 +0.002 (probe 31). But the finding's two main claims do not hold. (1) The float-output calibration is invalid. Probes 32/33 used the safe encoding w = round(v) + clip(frac, 0, 0.499). It was built so that a server that rounds coordinates gets back exactly the integer CSV. CONTEXT l.1499 left the tie unexplained ('server rounds, OR gain < 0.0005'). If the server rounds, both probes were literal no-ops on the LB, so they say nothing about how lab gains transfer, and 'transfer <= ~0.5 of lab' has no basis. exp75 writes integer voxel shifts (kernel integer path, up to 1.5 um at alpha 0.5), and those survive any server rounding. So it is not the same class on the one mechanism that could explain the tie. A better transfer record exists and points the same way: Eric's sub-voxel refinement had lab +0.0078 and LB -0.002 twice (v3 localisation value json). V1284's +0.002 is confounded by a -2.9% node drop. (2) The probability ignores the rounding edge. By rank in the block (6th of 113; round18 scan_hyp_slots_28sep), exp70b sits ~5e-5 below 0.9545 and K2 files ~1.6e-4 below it. A display >= 0.955 then needs only ~+0.0002 (~22 net edge flips), not +0.001. With the finding's own central transfer (0.5 x 0.00215 ~ +0.001), P(>= 0.955) would be > 0.5. That contradicts its 'P <= 0.3' and 'a tie is the expected result'. The honest odds depend on the SIGN of the effect on an unseen embryo, which the in-sample 4-clip lab cannot settle (1 of 4 clips negative, sign flip at a0.3). That gives P ~0.35-0.45, about what the 12:50Z check (0.35) and the slots plan for exp76a on exp70b (0.45) said. The pre-registration part (tie -> no rung; attributable UP -> one stack; <= 0.953 -> close) is sound, cheap and within R1-R10. 'No alpha/MAX_UM rung' is already covered by the team rule against public knob ladders. Finals #37/#38 are unaffected. Private value: unknown to slightly negative. The refiner was trained on train embryos, and annotation-convention bias on new embryos is the dominant risk, so a public UP should not by itself re-tick finals.
